tallyf(1) — Linux manual page

NAME

tallyf - count and summarize delimited fields

SYNOPSIS

tallyf [-d delim] [-f list] [--json] [file ...]

DESCRIPTION

tallyf reads lines from each file, or from standard input when no file is given, and splits every line on a delimiter. It then counts how often each distinct value appears in the selected fields, and prints the counts in descending order.

Unlike a pipeline of cut, sort and uniq, tallyf keeps only one table of counts in memory, so it handles very large inputs without temporary files. Lines with fewer fields than requested are skipped, and a warning is printed once per file.

Output is plain text by default, with one value per line, followed by a tab and its count. With --json, a single JSON object is printed instead, which is easier to feed into other programs.

OPTIONS

-d delim
Use delim as the field separator. The default is a tab character.
-f list
Select fields by number, starting at 1. Ranges such as 2-4 and lists such as 1,3 are accepted.
--json
Print the result as JSON.

EXIT STATUS

Exit status is 0 on success, 1 if any input file could not be read, and 2 on invalid options.

EXAMPLES

$ tallyf -d , -f 3 orders.csv | head -n 3
shipped	1824
pending	311
returned	27

SEE ALSO

cut(1), sort(1), uniq(1)
